title: Ops Anchor: weekly thread & resolution notes — 2027-03-14
content:
Context and purpose:
This is the weekly SRE 'ops-anchor' thread covering on-call handoffs, incident summaries, SLO deviations, and short-term remediation steps. Designed to be a compact single-page read for the next oncall and engineering leads.

High-level summary (week of 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-14):
- Total page(s) of noise: 1 pager.
- Incidents: 2 P1/P2-ish events that required cross-team coordination.
- SLOs: token-gen latency SLO (p95) breached twice during peak traffic windows; overall error-rate SLO still within tolerance.
- Key operational changes: early rollout of warmstart autoscaler to limited region (staging -> us-west-2 canary), small KV-cache eviction thresholds adjusted, preliminary canary rollback automation added to release job.

Incident digest:
1) INC-2027-032 — KV cache churn causing tail-latency spikes (2027-03-10 09:12 UTC)
   - Symptom: p99/p95 for text-generation spiked ~600ms above baseline; customer-facing traces showed repeated KV cache misses and rehydration.
   - Impact: ~7% of production requests in us-west-2 experienced >2s response time for ~26 minutes. No data loss.
   - Root cause hypothesis: a background GC/eviction job misfired when node memory pressure briefly exceeded threshold after a large batch of short-context requests; eviction threshold logic inadvertently evicted more prefixes than expected.
   - Mitigation steps taken:
     * Rollback of the new eviction tuning to previous safe settings (by oncall, 09:22 UTC).
     * Cache priming script executed for hot prefixes to reduce immediate misses (SRE runbook step).
     * Temporary routing of heavy customers to dedicated pool while we validated rollback (10:05 UTC).
   - Follow-ups / owners:
     * infra/serving runtime to add a guardrail: prevent bulk-eviction unless under sustained high memory pressure (owner: Liam Patel, due 2027-03-21).
     * Add a test in staging that simulates short-context fanout to exercise eviction path (owner: Sofia Martinez, due 2027-03-18).
     * Runbook update: explicitly include cache priming and routing fallback steps (owner: Maya Chen, due 2027-03-17).

2) INC-2027-034 — transient OOM on older CPU fallback nodes during model rollout (2027-03-12 02:40 UTC)
   - Symptom: Several fallback nodes (cpu-fallback-*) OOMed after a spike in low-concurrency, long-context requests during a model variant rollout. Auto-restart loops caused increased error 5xx rate for ~12 minutes.
   - Impact: 5xx spike but automated fallback to hosted API model variant worked; latency increased for some routes.
   - Immediate mitigation:
     * Canary rollback of model variant rollout (deployment aborted, 02:56 UTC).
     * Increased the soft cap and configured a linear warmstart to reduce cold memory allocations on fallback nodes (03:10 UTC).
   - Root cause & action items:
     * Serving runtime should detect model packing changes and avoid co-locating multiple heavy KV contexts on CPU fallback nodes (owner: Daniel Okafor, due 2027-03-28).
     * Add preflight that validates memory footprint delta for new model artifacts in the deployment pipeline (owner: release-eng, due 2027-03-24).

SLO snapshot and interpretation:
- Token-gen latency p95 (global): target 450ms. Observed p95 peaks at 1.05s during the KV cache incident (mar 10). Weekly avg p95: 420ms.
- Error rate (5xx) SLO: target <0.5% per day. Observed brief spike to 0.9% during OOM incident; daily average remains 0.18%.
- Business note: One enterprise customer flagged latency regressions in support ticket TKT-9843. We coordinated with Solutions to provide mitigation and temporary routing — customer satisfied with workaround.

Operational experiments and tuning notes:
- Warmstart autoscaler (limited canary)
  * Purpose: reduce cold-start allocations and node churn during bursty, low-concurrency requests.
  * Outcome: staging tests show 18% reduction in cold-start 95th latency; canary in us-west-2 shows promising resource stability but needs more traffic.
  * Next step: expand canary to two additional non-critical regions, monitor memory pressure metrics and tail latency for 48 hours (owner: infra-autoscale, due 2027-03-22).

- Autoscaler decision heuristics tweak applied (rollback-able)
  * Short-term tweak reduced aggressive downscaling window which likely contributed to cache churn. We reverted the tweak after INC-032. Plan to run a controlled AB test in staging instead of global flip.

Runbook & playbook changes (short list):
- Add explicit steps for "cache priming" in the "KV cache eviction" playbook.
- Add a pre-deploy memory delta check for model artifacts in the release pipeline.
- Add two new PagerDuty alert conditions: 
  * kv_cache_evictions.rate > 10/min for >5 min (severity: page)
  * cpu_fallback.oom_count > 1 in 5 min (severity: page)
  Owners: monitoring (alerting) team to implement (owner: Natalia Rivers, due 2027-03-20).

On-call handoff notes (next shift):
- Current oncall: Maya Chen (until 2027-03-15 08:00 UTC)
- Incoming oncall: Liam Patel (2027-03-15 08:00 UTC onward)
- Critical reminders for incoming oncall:
  * Watch kv_cache.eviction.rate and p95 token-gen during 08:30-11:30 UTC window — historic peak traffic.
  * If KV cache eviction threshold triggers, follow "Cache priming" runbook before any cluster-wide eviction changes.
  * If OOM spike occurs on cpu-fallback, abort rollouts and enable linear warmstart scaling.
  * Contact list: Release eng (pager: #releases), Infra (slack: @infra-ops), Solutions (slack: #solutions-escalations).

Meeting & sync items for next week:
- Post-incident retrospective (INC-2027-032 and INC-2027-034) — scheduled 2027-03-18 16:00 UTC. Invitees: SRE, Serving-runtime, Release-engineering, Solutions. Outcome: actionable postmortem doc and a decision on eviction guardrails.
- Autoscaler tuning review 2027-03-19 09:00 UTC — present canary telemetry (owner: infra-autoscale).
- Runbook dry-run session 2027-03-20 14:00 UTC — bring a fresh engineer to follow the cache priming steps and confirm clarity.

Action item table (compact):
- Add eviction guardrail (Liam Patel) — due 2027-03-21
- Staging short-context eviction test (Sofia Martinez) — due 2027-03-18
- Runbook update for cache priming (Maya Chen) — due 2027-03-17
- Preflight memory delta in pipeline (release-eng) — due 2027-03-24
- PagerDuty alert creation (Natalia Rivers) — due 2027-03-20
- Warmstart canary expansion (infra-autoscale) — due 2027-03-22

Notes to readers / freeform thoughts:
- Two incidents in one week with overlapping memory-pressure signals suggest we should invest in a small observability project to correlate eviction, GC, and autoscaler decisions at the node-level. This could be a 2–3 sprint task but would reduce time-to-detect for similar incidents.
- Consider a "gradual eviction" experimental knob that triggers partial prefix sweeps instead of whole-shard drops. Might be implemented as a runtime flag first.

Appendix / quick links:
- KV cache runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/kv-cache-runbook-draft
- INC-2027-032 ticket: JIRA-INC-2027-032
- INC-2027-034 ticket: JIRA-INC-2027-034
- PR for rollback automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

End of ops-anchor thread. Please add inline comments if you have updates or corrections.
